items.q: Dysphagia with immediate coughing, nasal regurgitation and recurrent pneumonias localises where?
items.exp: Failure to protect airway and propel bolus from pharynx causes instant symptoms and aspiration pneumonia (stroke, Parkinson, MND), needing swallow filming and therapy, not primary oesophageal dilation.
r: Incorrect. Distal disease delays symptoms seconds.
Incorrect. Gastric issues vomit and pain.
items.kp: Chokes on first move: throat phase broken.

items.q: Progressive solids only dysphagia over 3 months with 8 kg loss in 65 year old smoker needs what urgently?
o: Urgent upper GI endoscopy (cancer exclusion) with imaging pathway
items.exp: Alarm dysphagia (progressive mechanical pattern, weight loss, age) mandates urgent scope and biopsies for oesophageal or gastric cardia cancer, staging CT if confirmed. Functional labels are forbidden here.
items.kp: Sticking plus shrinking equals scope now.

items.q: Dysphagia solids and liquids from onset, regurgitation and bird beak barium outline indicate what?
items.exp: Achalasia loses myenteric neurons causing non relaxing lower sphincter and absent peristalsis; barium shows dilated oesophagus tapering beak, manometry confirms. Cancer pseudoachalasia mimics in older short history patients needing scope.
r: Incorrect. Cancer favours solids progressive shorter.
Incorrect. Web is high thin membrane solids only.
items.kp: Both phases blocked, beak below: achalasia.

items.q: Elderly man regurgitates undigested food hours later, halitosis and gurgling neck swelling suggest what and diagnostic test?
items.exp: Pharyngeal pouch through Killian dehiscence stores food causing delayed regurgitation, aspiration and Boerhaave risk with blind instrumentation; barium outlines it, endoscopic stapling divides common wall.
r: Incorrect. Achalasia retains in chest with dysphagia both.
Incorrect. Globus lacks regurgitation and swelling.
Incorrect. Endoscopy first can perforate pouch.
items.kp: Old food returns undigested: Zenker pouch.

items.q: Iron deficiency anaemia, glossitis and postcricoid web causing dysphagia in middle aged woman is which syndrome?
items.exp: Plummer Vinson triad (iron deficiency, oesophageal webs, dysphagia) carries postcricoid carcinoma risk needing iron replacement, dilation and surveillance endoscopy.
r: Incorrect. Achalasia lacks iron web triad.
Incorrect. Barrett is distal metaplasia reflux.
Incorrect. Mallory Weiss tears bleed after retching.
items.kp: No iron, sore tongue, web: Plummer Vinson.

items.q: Young atopic man with intermittent solid food impaction (steakhouse episodes) and rings on endoscopy most likely has what?
items.exp: Eosinophilic oesophagitis in allergic young males causes rings (trachealisation), furrows and strictures with food bolus arrests; biopsies (over 15 eosinophils per high power pattern) despite normal look, treated dietary elimination, topical swallowed steroids or PPIs pathways.
r: Incorrect. Schatzki is single mucosal ring older pattern.
Correct. Eosinophilic oesophagitis of atopic youth.
Incorrect. Liquids also fail in achalasia.
Incorrect. Age and intermittence argue against.

items.q: Silent aspiration means what and in whom is it classic worry?
o: Aspiration with violent cough in healthy
Aspiration without cough or sensation, in neurological disease and post stroke or Parkinson
items.exp: Lost laryngeal sensation lets material pass cords silently, so absence of coughing falsely reassures in neurogenic dysphagia; instrumental swallow studies (FEES, videofluoroscopy) reveal it guiding diet safety.
r: Incorrect. Violent cough is protective aspiration.
items.kp: No cough does not mean no aspiration.

items.q: Globus sensation is best defined how and managed after normal examination?
o: Food sticking with weight loss; scope yearly forever
Lump feeling between meals without dysphagia or alarm, reassurance plus reflux and tension measures
items.exp: Globus pharyngeus peaks between meals, swallowing food often eases it, and lacks alarm features; explanation, reflux lifestyle or therapy and laryngeal tension speech therapy settle most, investigating only red flags.
r: Correct. Between meals lump, no alarm.
Incorrect. Pain is odynophagia different problem.
items.kp: Lump when not eating, eats fine: globus.

items.q: Painful swallowing (odynophagia) with white plaques in immunocompromised patient suggests what first?
items.exp: Odynophagia dominant over dysphagia in HIV or steroid hosts points infective oesophagitis; candida commonest, endoscopy distinguishes viral ulcers when empiric fluconazole fails.
r: Incorrect. Cancer aches progressively with solids pattern.
items.kp: Painful swallow plus immune down: candida.

items.q: Schatzki ring causes which classic episodic pattern?
o: Intermittent solid (meat, bread) impaction at lower oesophageal mucosal ring, steakhouse syndrome
items.exp: A thin mucosal ring at squamocolumnar junction intermittently arrests poorly chewed meat boluses between long normal intervals, dilated at endoscopy after bolus clearance; eosinophilic disease must be biopsied in young.
r: Correct. Episodic meat arrest, Schatzki ring.
